subject: Post-call recap: procurement path & trial success criteria — AuroraSoft
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@aurorasoft.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@aurorasoft.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 14:07:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: procurement path & trial success criteria — AuroraSoft

Hi Jane / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on procurement and the trial-to-paid path.

Key points from the call:
- Procurement preference: AuroraSoft indicated procurement prefers starting with a PO invoicing flow (Net 30) and vendor onboarding via their AP portal. Card payment is acceptable for the pilot but they want long-term invoicing for production.
- Marketplace: They are evaluating whether to purchase via the Cloud Marketplace (for centralized billing) vs. direct vendor PO. Marketplace would simplify some procurement approvals but might add a 6–8 week listing review cadence.
- Trial scope & success criteria: 2-week pilot across 3 teams (Search, Summaries, Recommendations). Success criteria we agreed on:
  * 95th pct latency under 250ms for inference paths in Search test harness
  * >0.85 precision in generated summaries on the baseline eval set
  * Sustained allowlisted throughput of 5000 tokens/min during peak window
- Billing start: AuroraSoft prefers billing to begin once pilot success criteria are met and a PO is signed for the initial committed capacity. We proposed an alternative: start billing on a calendar date if delivery milestones slip.

Attachments I uploaded: Redwood-Quote-v1.pdf (draft pricing + committed capacity table), Procurement-Checklist.xlsx (vendor onboarding items), Mutual-Action-Plan-aurorasoft.csv (high-level timeline).

Proposed next steps (action owners & ETA):
1) Grace — update quote to include PO invoicing option and marketplace notes; send by 05/11.
2) Jane — introduce procurement@aurorasoft.com to our quoting team and share vendor onboarding SLA; intro expected by 05/10.
3) Marissa — prepare a one-pager on marketplace tradeoffs (pricing flow, fees, timeline) by 05/12.
4) Connor — standby to do a brief pilot runbook and baseline scripts for latency/throughput tests; ready by 05/13.

Please reply if I missed anything or if we should re-prioritize items.

Thanks —
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: procurement path & trial success criteria — AuroraSoft

Hi Grace —

Thanks for the clear notes — this matches our discussion. A few clarifications from procurement side:
- Procurement prefers a PO + invoice (Net 30) for anything that will be capitalized into production. For pilots under $10k we can typically use a company card to speed things up.
- Marketplace purchase is attractive to product finance, but procurement needs to confirm whether the marketplace contract allows for our liability and data controls. That is a gating question.
- On success criteria: the metrics look good. We'll also want an availability SLO for the pilot window (99.5% uptime target) — can Redwood commit to monitoring and brief escalation routing during the two-week run?

Action: I copied procurement@aurorasoft.com — they will review the Procurement-Checklist and confirm required documents. Procurement asked if Redwood can accept a vendor form with a standard 60-day vendor onboarding timeframe (they try to compress it for pilots, but it can take longer).

Jane
Director of Product — AuroraSoft
jane.doe@aurorasoft.com | +1 (650) 555-4444
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: procurement path & trial success criteria — AuroraSoft

Grace / Jane —

Quick marketplace note: if AuroraSoft prefers to go the marketplace route, two items to call out for procurement:
- Marketplace listing fee and platform margin (typically 5–8%) — we'll surface this on a comparison table so finance can see landed cost.
- Billing cadence: Marketplaces sometimes force billing through the buyer's marketplace account and can change invoice terms; if AuroraSoft needs Net 30 by contract, we should validate whether marketplace invoicing preserves those terms.

I uploaded a short one-pager (not attached here in thread) and will drop the comparison doc into the HubSpot deal record by EOD 05/12.

Also: Grace, can you confirm whether Redwood can provide an uptime monitoring link and a named escalation contact for the pilot? If so, I'll add that to the pilot runbook.

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: procurement path & trial success criteria — AuroraSoft

Thanks, everyone — closing the loop here with confirmations and updated timeline.

Confirmed items:
- Redwood can support the PO + invoice Net 30 flow for the production contract. For the pilot, card payment is fine and will allow the trial to start earlier.
- We will provide an uptime dashboard (read-only link) and a named escalation contact (on-call SRE) for the pilot; Marissa will include the link and contact in the runbook by 05/13.
- If procurement requires vendor onboarding longer than 30 days, we can still start the pilot on card and invoice once the PO is approved for production capacity.

Updated mutual action plan and dates:
- 05/11: Grace to send updated quote with PO invoicing line-item (DONE).
- 05/12: Marissa to upload marketplace comparison doc to HubSpot (IN PROGRESS).
- 05/13: Connor to post pilot runbook and test harness (PENDING).
- 05/17: Target pilot start date (card-funded). Pilot length: 14 days.
- Billing commencement: Billing to start on the earlier of (a) PO-signed date for committed capacity, or (b) 05/31 if pilot success criteria met and PO remains in process.

Please reply with objections; if none, I'll send a DocuSign for the PO terms and the pilot agreement next week (link in related_links).

Best —
Grace
